transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Morris (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Gomez (Lighthouse Head of Procurement), Ethan Li (Lighthouse CISO), Dr. Priya Narang (Lighthouse ML Platform)

Summary:
Redwood and Lighthouse Health ran a procurement/onboarding call to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA requirements for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing approval timelines, and technical benchmark scheduling. Customer requested SOC 2 artifacts, KMS/HSM options, audit log retention details, and an initial performance benchmark plan. Next steps and action items were agreed.

Topics:
- MSA and DPA redline process and legal owners
- SLA targets (p95/p99 latency, uptime, support response times)
- Pricing approval timeline and pilot discounts
- Private deployment (VPC) and KMS/HSM integration
- Benchmark plan for latency/cost tradeoffs and quantization recommendations

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna Morris: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you fitting this in. I'm Jenna at Redwood, with Ravi from our SE team. How're you all doing?
[00:10] Marta Gomez: Good, thanks. We have about an hour, should be enough to go through the DPA and the SLAs. I'll let Ethan and Priya jump in on the security and tech parts.
[00:18] Ethan Li: Yep, thanks Marta. Hi Jenna, Ravi. Quick ask up front: we need to understand what audit logs look like, retention, and what KMS integration you support, like HSM or customer-managed keys.
[00:30] Ravi Patel: Sure, Ethan. We support customer-managed keys via common KMS providers; we also have an on-prem HSM option for Private deployments. In the hosted flow, you can opt for a customer-supplied key and we produce audit logs — format is JSON by default, with retention configurable if you buy extended observability.
[00:45] Priya Narang: Can you be specific about the audit events? We need token-level usage, per-route latencies, and per-model inference traces for our compliance team.
[00:55] Ravi Patel: Yep, we capture token-level cost and latency breakdowns, model route tracing and error logs. Small caveat, in hosted there is an aggregated retention policy unless you get the observability addon.
[01:06] Marta Gomez: On the legal side, our counsel will send redlines to the MSA and DPA. What's your SLAs section look like by default? We need to know your standard uptime and support response times so we can map to our vendor approval matrix.
[01:20] Jenna Morris: Our standard hosted SLA covers 99.5% uptime for API, with support response within 4 business hours for P1s on standard plan; Dedicated has stronger SLAs — 99.9% and a 1 hour P1 response if you commit to reserved capacity. We can provide a doc that maps SLA tiers to contract language.
[01:36] Ethan Li: 99.9% is okay but we care about p95/p99 latency guarantees for critical flows. Is that something you can commit in Dedicated?
[01:45] Ravi Patel: We usually provide latency SLOs based on model class and instance type. For Dedicated, we can target p95 under 200ms for our small chat models on common GPU profiles; p99 is a bit more variable, depends on sequence length and batching — we'll include specific profiles in the SLA annex.
[02:02] Priya Narang: Is there a way to force fallbacks to cheaper model variants if capacity is constrained? We want graceful degradation for patient-facing flows.
[02:12] Jenna Morris: Yes, smart routing and fallback policies are supported. You can pin rollouts and set automated fallbacks to compatible variants — we can include recommended configs in the deployment runbook.
[02:23] Marta Gomez: Pricing — our finance needs a clear pilot discount and then a committed pricing for Dedicated if we move forward. Timeline: legal review this week, pricing approval next week, we hope to sign pilot by end of April.
[02:37] Jenna Morris: For pilots we typically offer trial credits and a short-term pilot discount; for Dedicated we can structure a reserved capacity quote. I'll send the pricing spreadsheet and a proposed commit plan after the call.
[02:48] Ethan Li: Security: can you confirm SOC 2 type II and ISO-27001? Also, do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[02:58] Ravi Patel: We are SOC 2 Type II and ISO-27001 certified — I will share the attestation. We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in both Hosted and Private. For Private deployments, you get network isolation + customer-managed keys.
[03:12] Marta Gomez: Great. About the DPA — any data residency options? For some patient data we need EU residency.
[03:20] Jenna Morris: We have region controls; hosted customers can select the region and we can discuss contractual data residency clauses. For strict residency we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated in a chosen region.
[03:30] Priya Narang: About benchmarks — can we schedule a hands-on benchmark where we run our sample traffic? We'll need terraform snippets and a runbook.
[03:38] Ravi Patel: Absolutely. We'll provide terraform examples for Dedicated and hosted test harnesses. For the benchmark, we'll want your traffic profile and target latency/cost goals. We'll run a 2–3 day test and return a result set with token cost estimates and quantization recommendations.
[03:55] Marta Gomez: Legal would like to see indemnity and data handling language — is your standard MSA fairly vendor-favorable or do you accept customer redlines?
[04:03] Jenna Morris: We review redlines case-by-case. For typical enterprise customers we accept reasonable redlines on the DPA and some MSA clauses; extreme indemnity requests usually trigger legal escalation. We'll accept your redlines and aim to respond within 3 business days.
[04:16] Ethan Li: One concern: we evaluated an internal self-host approach and Anthropic; our security team thinks self-host gives most control but increases ops burden. What tradeoffs should we call out for Redwood?
[04:28] Ravi Patel: The tradeoff is ops vs economics. Self-host gives you control over keys and networking but you inherit maintenance and model updates. Redwood aims to provide predictable economics, fallback policies, and operational tooling so you don't have to build the infra. We'll share a short doc comparing hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs.
[04:44] Priya Narang: Also want to understand quantization and model quality regressions — do you have eval hooks?
[04:50] Jenna Morris: Yes, we have Redwood Optimize that recommends quantization profiles and eval pipelines. We also support prompt sets and regression alerts tied to evals. We'll share a sample eval report.
[05:00] Marta Gomez: Ok let's recap next steps. Jenna, you'll send the MSA/DPA redline contact and pricing spreadsheet; Ravi will send SOC2/ISO artifacts, terraform snippets, and benchmark plan. We'll try to get legal comments by 2026-04-13.
[05:14] Jenna Morris: Correct — I'll get the docs over today/tomorrow and include a proposed SLA annex language for Dedicated.
[05:20] Ethan Li: I'll confirm audit log retention requirements and share them by 2026-04-15.
[05:25] Priya Narang: I'll pull sample traffic and target latencies by 2026-04-17.
[05:30] Jenna Morris: Great. Any last Qs?
[05:34] Marta Gomez: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[05:38] Jenna Morris: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email, expect the MSA/DPA redline and pricing spreadsheet.

End of call.
